entries.reconstructed_theorem: Let E be any complete real inner product space and let f:E→ℝ be continuously Fréchet differentiable and convex on all of E. Let β be strictly positive real number β. Assume that for every x,y∈E, f(y) ≤ f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖², where ∇f(x) is the Riesz vector representing the Fréchet derivative. Then for every x,y∈E, ‖∇f(y)−∇f(x)‖² ≤ 2β(f(y)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩).
entries.reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner product space and let f:E→ℝ be continuously Fréchet differentiable and convex on all of E. Let β be strictly positive real number β. Assume that for every x,y∈E, f(y) ≤ f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖², where ∇f(x) is the Riesz vector representing the Fréchet derivative. Then for every x,y∈E, ‖∇f(y)−∇f(x)‖² ≤ 2β(f(y)−f(x)−⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩).
entries.objects: E, a real inner product space with its compatible norm and additive group; f:E→ℝ; β; the gradient ∇f:E→E representing the Fréchet derivative; arbitrary points x,y.
entries.domains: E is complete, of any universe and with no finite-dimensional restriction; f is defined on all E; values and inner products are real; β∈ℝ with β>0.
entries.quantifiers: Universally for every such E, every f:E→ℝ and every admissible β, the stated assumptions imply the conclusion. The upper quadratic bound quantifies independently over all x,y∈E; the conclusion also holds for all x,y∈E.
entries.assumptions: E is a normed additive commutative group and real inner product space, and is complete. f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on E and convex on E. β>0. For all x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖².
entries.scopes: Both assumptions on f and the two-point quadratic upper bound are global on E. The same f and same β occur throughout. Convexity is the chord inequality on the entire space. There is no restriction to a subset, probability space, or finite dimension.
entries.constant_dependencies: The coefficient is exactly 2β and depends only on the positive real β appearing in the assumed quadratic bound.
